races.title: State Assembly, District 5
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Neva Parker
cands.bio: Democratic candidate for California Assembly District 5 (Placer and El Dorado Counties). Worked 26 years as nonpartisan California legislative staff, including as Senate Journal Clerk. Co-owned several small businesses with her husband. Lives in Roseville. Ran for the same seat in 2024.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, Equality California, California Young Democrats and the California Mountain Biking Coalition.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Neva Parker on data centers, development or growth limits, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land, immigration or H-1B, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. Her campaign site is general on public safety; it only says she would work to fund Proposition 36 treatment programs and courts. She has never held elected office, so there is no voting record. We found no news coverage of controversies. Her birthplace is given as Richmond by Ballotpedia and as Hercules in her own materials, so we could not pin down the exact city.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as Richmond, CA, and her campaign says she was born and raised in Hercules, so both put her birth and upbringing in California; she has lived in Roseville for about 22 years.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Spent 26 years as nonpartisan California legislative staff, starting as a Capitol intern and rising to Senate Journal Clerk, where she kept the Senate's official record. She also co-owned several retail and online nutrition businesses. She has not held elected office.
qual.why: A long career inside the legislative process and small-business ownership put her in the middle-to-upper part of the range. She has no prior legislative service as a member and no documented budget or policy-writing role. Her advisory commission seats are not counted.
qual.label: A long career inside the legislative process and small-business ownership put her in the middle-to-upper part of the range. She has no prior legislative service as a member and no documented budget or policy-writing role. Her advisory commission seats are not counted.

clean-money.evidence: Her campaign site says she is a "corporate-free candidate" who does not accept money from corporations.

cands.name: Joe Patterson
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 5 since December 2022. Former Rocklin city councilmember (2016–2022) and mayor (2019). Began his career as a Jesse M. Unruh Assembly Fellow, worked in public policy, and was executive director of the California Gaming Association.

endorsements.text: Republican Party of California; International Union of Operating Engineers Local 3; Reform California; YIMBY Action (2026 endorsements listed on Ballotpedia)
Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association (stated on his campaign site)

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Patterson on data centers, on limits for investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, on H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, on gun laws, on abortion, or on school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented stance on development or growth limits beyond a general pledge to protect local quality of life. Legislation he sponsored is only described on his campaign site, and we could not open the bill texts to check what each bill does. His birth year, and any time he lived outside California, were not found. No controversies appeared in the pages we had.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Napa, California and graduated from Napa High School, and he has lived in Rocklin, California as an adult.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2022. Rocklin City Council 2016–2022, including a term as mayor in 2019. Began as an Unruh Assembly Fellow, worked in public policy, and was executive director of the California Gaming Association.
qual.why: He has prior legislative service in the Assembly, local elected office on a city council, and a policy career, which fits the rubric's high range for writing law and budgets.
qual.label: He has prior legislative service in the Assembly, local elected office on a city council, and a policy career, which fits the rubric's high range for writing law and budgets.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight to protect Prop 13, the law that limits homeowner property tax increases, and cites an endorsement from the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association. It does not call for eliminating homestead taxes.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he strongly supports local law enforcement, wants criminals held accountable and officers fully equipped, and says nearly every local and statewide law enforcement organization endorses him.
